course_name_en: Selection and Dimensioning of Machine Elements
prerequisites: applied mechanics: equilibrium of statically determinate systems in a three-dimensional space, kinematics of planar motion, and dynamics in planar motion
strength of materials: stress calculation in rods and beams with a solid section under normal force, under shear force, under bending, and in rods with an axisymmetric section under torsion
materials science: elastic material behavior in a uniaxial stress state, yield strength

learning_outcomes.text: The student understands the functioning of a machine and its components and can independently perform dimensioning calculations.

The student knows the main groups of machine components. They can reason and describe the function of the component in the operation of a machine. They can perform a comparative study and select an appropriate component.

The student can establish a link between the application principles of a machine component and the basic concepts from mechanics that underpin them. They can perform an analysis of the force action in the machine and the component, and of the component's movement. They can apply the models and calculation principles from mechanics, using the approximations common for machine components.
The student can consult catalogs of machine components and retrieve the data relevant for dimensioning a component.

syllabus_topics: Machine components and principles of dimensioning for strength, stiffness, and fatigue
Joining techniques: welding, rivet joints, and bolted joints
Transmission shafts: statically determinate and statically indeterminate
Components of transmission systems: bearings, couplings
0. Basic principles of strength of materials and dimensioning (6 hours)
Overview of the main principles from strength of materials for calculation of internal forces, stresses and deformations of rods and beams
Specifications for dimensioning for strength and stiffness
Statically determinate shafts: strength and stiffness
4. Components of transmission systems: rolling bearings (1 hour)
0. Basic principles of strength of materials and dimensioning (2 hours)
Application of the main principles from strength of materials: determination of diagrams of internal forces
Calculation of section properties and stresses
Statically determinate shafts: strength and stiffness
4. Components of transmission systems: rolling bearings (1 hour)
teaching_methods: Practicum (solving assignments individually or in groups)
Seminars (description of component function, selection, and dimensioning principles; solving assignments; compulsory attendance and active participation)

assessment_methods.method: Collected assignments from seminars (for students who did not attend seminars)

assessment_rules: The exam is written with an oral explanation. Students may use the Roloff-Matek Machine-onderdelen textbook and tables book, unannotated. Each student receives three major questions, one each on joining techniques, transmission shafts, and transmissions, with sub-questions on dimensional tolerances and rolling bearings. Two of the three questions include an individual oral discussion after written preparation, while the third is only written. The three questions are weighted equally; in case of deficiencies on at least two questions, rounding is always downwards. For students who actively attended the seminars, the material covered in the seminars is excluded from the exam. Students who missed one or more seminars will receive an additional written question from the missed seminar(s) to be submitted within the same time frame.
